Trace, implement and test: 03.03.Stack of Plates

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
class StackOfPlates {
public:
    StackOfPlates(int cap) {
        this->cap = cap;
    }

    void push(int val) {
        if (!cap) {
            return;
        }
        if (stk.empty() || stk.back().size() >= cap) {
            stk.emplace_back(stack<int>());
        }
        stk.back().push(val);
    }

    int pop() {
        return popAt(stk.size() - 1);
    }

    int popAt(int index) {
        int ans = -1;
        if (index >= 0 && index < stk.size()) {
            ans = stk[index].top();
            stk[index].pop();
            if (stk[index].empty()) {
                stk.erase(stk.begin() + index);
            }
        }
        return ans;
    }

private:
    int cap;
    vector<stack<int>> stk;
};

/**
 * Your StackOfPlates object will be instantiated and called as such:
 * StackOfPlates* obj = new StackOfPlates(cap);
 * obj->push(val);
 * int param_2 = obj->pop();
 * int param_3 = obj->popAt(index);
 */
